snippet.description:
Thinking about moving to Thailand in 2026? Stop. The game has changed.

Thailand isn't the same country it was five years ago. The rules have tightened, the "cheap" lifestyle is a myth for most, and the days of winging it on a tourist visa are fading fast. If you are planning to quit your job, sell your stuff, and move to Bangkok or Pattaya thinking it will solve all your problems—you are walking into a trap.

In this video, I’m giving you the hard truth about what it actually takes to survive (and thrive) here in 2026. No sugar-coating, no "paradise" fluff. Just the reality of visas, money, dating, and the mindset you need to make it work.

In this video, we cover:

The Visa Crackdown: Why immigration is asking more questions and why the "border run" lifestyle is dying.

The "Cheap" Myth: The real cost of living when you factor in rent creep, dating, and convenience addiction.

The Dating Trap: Why getting attention isn't the same as finding a partner, and how loneliness drives expensive mistakes.

The Expat Reality: Why Thailand amplifies your problems instead of fixing them.

Beaches: Less crowded and more peaceful than Hua Hin’s beaches.

snippet.title: Pacific Cross Health Insurance Interview part 1
snippet.description:
Pacific Cross Health Insurance offers a range of health, travel and accident insurance plans in Thailand designed for residents, expatriates, and travelers. Coverage depends on the plan you choose, but generally includes the following:

🏥 Health Insurance Coverage

A variety of plans from basic to comprehensive, with annual benefit limits up to several million USD/THB depending on the tier.

Inpatient coverage for hospital stays, surgeries, diagnostics, and treatment costs.

Outpatient benefits and maternity care on many plans (e.g., Standard, Comprehensive).

Cashless direct billing at a large network of hospitals in Thailand and ASEAN to minimize upfront costs.

Emergency medical and evacuation coverage including worldwide emergency treatment.

Pre‑existing conditions coverage available under specialized Expat Care plans after a waiting period.

Lifetime renewability with no age limit on many plans.

🌏 Travel & Visa Insurance

Plans for short trips (e.g., Bon Voyage Single‑Trip) and annual coverage for frequent travelers.

Long‑stay/visa compliant policies that meet Thailand’s minimum health insurance requirements for certain visa types.

snippet.title: I Left the U.S for Thailand... Here's Why
snippet.description:
I didn’t move to Thailand for the beaches or the cheap living.
I moved because life back home stopped feeling like life.

After years of doing everything “right” in the U.S. career, apartment, insurance, the grind, something still felt off. I couldn’t name it at the time, but I felt constantly tired. Not physically… just tired of existing.

This video isn’t about paradise or escape. It’s about peace. It’s about what happens when you finally slow down long enough to realize how much pressure you’ve been carrying without noticing.

If you’ve ever felt that quiet exhaustion, like you’re living on autopilot, this one might hit home.

snippet.title: This Emerald Pool in Thailand Looks Fake… But It’s Real (Krabi)

In this video, we explore the Emerald Pool and the Khlong Thom Hot Springs, two of the most unique natural experiences near Ao Nang. What started as a simple day trip turned into a full jungle adventure with glowing emerald water, geothermal springs, and moments that completely surprised us.

If you’re a digital nomad, tourist, travel-loving couple, or planning a trip to Krabi, this video gives you a real sense of what to expect beyond the photos. From swimming in crystal-clear natural pools to soaking in steaming jungle hot springs, this is one of those days that feels unreal while you’re living it.

We visit the Emerald Pool early, explore deeper into the national park, and then end the day relaxing at the Klong Thom Hot Springs, where naturally heated water flows through the jungle like a spa. It’s calm, raw, and completely different from the beach scenes most people associate with Thailand.

This isn’t a tour brochure version of Thailand.
It’s what the experience actually feels like when you explore on your own, move at your own pace, and let the day unfold naturally.

Whether you’re:

Building a Krabi itinerary

Looking for unique things to do near Ao Nang

Wondering if the Emerald Pool and Klong Thom Hot Springs are worth visiting

snippet.title: My Accidental Tour WON Thailand's Top Award
snippet.description:
It started as an accident. A friend, a longtail boat, and getting completely lost in a breathtaking Thai mangrove forest. Years later, that "accident" has led to this incredible moment: my friend Sam Goodey and his team at Discovery Travel being honored with one of Thailand's most prestigious tourism awards, presented by a member of the Thai Royal Family.

This video tells the story of how a small, passionate tour operator in Khao Lak went from a simple idea to being recognized on a national stage. We were thrilled to travel to Bangkok to watch Sam accept a Silver Award at the 14th Thailand Tourism Awards 2023 for his outstanding contribution to the industry. These awards, known as the Kinnari Awards, are the gold standard for tourism in the country, and the ceremony was a spectacular event. The highlight, of course, was seeing the award presented by Her Royal Highness Princess Ubolratana Rajakanya Sirivadhana Barnavadi, a truly unforgettable honor that validates the hard work and passion behind their project.

But what makes this award so special? It wasn't won for a mega-resort or a high-volume tour. It was won for the Tha Din Daeng Community Tour, an intimate, sustainable, and deeply authentic kayaking adventure through the "Mangrove Maze" near Khao Lak.

As you'll see in the video, this is community-based tourism at its finest. The tours are run, operated, and led by the local community members themselves, with incredible guides like Nai sharing their ancestral knowledge of the waterways. Every aspect of the tour—from navigating the tides to pointing out wildlife, making tie-dye from natural materials, and even searching for tin in the sandbanks—is designed to be sustainable and to ensure the maximum benefit goes directly back to the village. This isn't just about showing tourists a beautiful place; it's about empowering a community to protect their environment and share their culture in a meaningful way.

This award is proof that a different kind of tourism is not only possible but celebrated. It’s about moving away from the crowded, well-trodden paths and discovering the hidden gems that make Thailand so magical. It’s about connecting with real people, supporting small businesses, and leaving a place better than you found it.

So, if you're planning a trip to Khao Lak, Phuket, or Southern Thailand and want an experience that goes beyond the ordinary, we can't recommend Sam and his team at Discovery Travel enough. They have shown that you can build a successful business with heart, integrity, and a genuine love for the community you operate in.

If you’re planning a trip to Koh Lanta (or deciding between Koh Lanta vs Phuket / Krabi), this video shows what you can realistically expect from the island’s vibe, how getting around works, and why this quieter Thai island can be such a special stop for digital nomads and travel-loving couples.

We visit Following Giants Koh Lanta, an ethical elephant sanctuary in Thailand that follows strict standards (no touching, no feeding, no bathing, no riding). If you’ve been researching ethical elephant sanctuaries in Thailand and want to avoid places that are “ethical” in name only, you’ll want to see what we learned on the ground.

After that, we slow things down with classic island moments, then end the day at Time for Lime Koh Lanta, a Thai cooking class connected to an animal welfare center that supports rescued street dogs and cats. It’s part travel experience, part giving back, and one of the most unique things to do in Koh Lanta if you care about responsible travel.

This is a real Koh Lanta day vlog with practical travel insights, honest impressions, and a few surprises along the way.
